why: The register of suites that may not vanish from a run without the run going red.
A suite that fails to LOAD reports as one failing file while every assertion it owns
disappears from the totals, so the passing test count goes UP. On 2026-08-25 that
happened to the safeguarding-red suite -- since retired by owner decision, see below --
and the run stayed green while its subject had no guard on main at all. The suite is
gone; the failure mode it exposed is why this register exists and is not.
Enforced by scripts/suiteAttendanceReporter.js on every
unnarrowed run; the register itself is kept honest by src/testing/suiteAttendance.test.ts.
minimumTests is a MEASURED FLOOR. It is not a target and it is not a ceiling: adding
tests is always fine, and a floor left behind by growth is stale rather than wrong --
re-measure it upward whenever you notice. Lowering one, or removing an entry, is a
deliberate act that has to be argued for in the same change -- never a way to make a
red run green.
2026-09-24, OWNER DECISION: 'let's scrap all the visual rules ... let's start the rules
from scratch when we find somthing that we want to turn into a rule we will'. The
Golden Era aesthetic guards were archived to archive/visual-rules-2026-09-24/ and their
entries removed from this register. They policed a visual language the club is
replacing -- which material a surface wears, which rung a colour comes from, how large
type and targets must be, which vocabulary is frozen -- and the club's own identity
turns out to be black, red and white with a boxing-groundhog crest, not brass and
parchment. A rule defending a design decision we have abandoned is not protection.
What remains here are the suites that stop the app telling somebody something untrue.
2026-09-24, OWNER DECISION on the safeguarding red: 'delete red no need for it to be
excluded'. The reservation held #A81E22 and seven tokens for MEDICALLY_NOT_ALLOWED
alone, banned the literal from CSS and TS/TSX, and carried a 118-entry ledger of every
existing site where a red sat near a failure word. The club's own identity is black,
red and white, so the app could not wear its own colours. The hue monopoly and the
ledger are gone. What is NOT gone: --locked still exists and still means a medical
stop. Anything that needs a medical stop to stay distinguishable from an ordinary
error belongs in a test of that surface, not in a repository-wide colour ban.

suites.guards: locked / restricted / monitor / cleared must still be DEFINED by whatever theme is loaded. A state that resolves to nothing is invisible, and no component test catches it because jsdom does not apply the stylesheet. It is a contract on an INCOMING theme, so it is at its most load-bearing exactly while the design system is being replaced. FLOOR LOWERED 15 -> 5 on 2026-09-24, owner decision 'keep the outcome, drop the prescribed implementation': the ten removed assertions demanded an -ink pair per token, a class literally named .badge, text-transform uppercase on it, and a badge--<name> variant per token. Those dictate a component name, a token naming convention and a typographic treatment, and they blocked scoping a palette to the rebuilt coach board. The non-colour channel they claimed to protect is now asserted where it is observable -- 'a RED readiness band never wears the medical-stop rung' in components/coachWorkspaceHonesty.test.tsx checks the band renders as a WORD, which a .badge that is uppercase and empty never did.

A member's red or blue corner may never be mistakable for a safety state. Chroma below every rung, delta-E 20 from every rung and ink tint. The same harm as the reserved red, approached from the other side.

The plate laws, enforced on the bytes -- SOI and EOI present, byte-size window, 4:4:4 with 1x1 components, a long edge of at least 720px so a plate is never a thumbnail, filename orientation and never square. AGENT_KERNEL.md names this file as the gate. Three of the first attempts to get plates into this repository failed in ways no human reviewer could see. The four-geometry allow-list was retired by owner decision 2026-09-24 ('go general with the screens'); it refused a 1920x1080 wall plate and declared one geometry that no file ever used.

The guard on the thing twenty guards stand on. Twenty-one test files read the design system through readDesignSystemCss; if it ever returned an empty string every one of them would go green while checking nothing -- which is exactly what happened on 2026-08-23 to thirteen guards when ppbf.css became two @import lines.

The refusal vocabulary, and specifically that MEDICALLY_NOT_ALLOWED is the one red mark -- the render-side companion to safeguardingRedReservation. Covers training_hold and the five non-medical refusals as the states that must NOT read as a medical bar.

Every design-system class the app references must have a real rule behind it. Written because a merge deleted 1,562 lines of ppbf.css and nothing noticed: a browser silently ignores a class with no rule, so the app kept rendering against an empty stylesheet with every check green. Eight tests holding the whole sheet.

The front door. One component behind both /login and the /public sign-in popover -- every person who uses this platform passes through it -- and nothing rendered it until this file existed. Its own docblock records that losing these tests puts the front door back to having no test at all, which is precisely the disappearance this manifest exists to make loud.

The client role session: TTL and expiry, self-clearing, and isRoleSessionAllowed -- which, in its own words, is what every page guard runs. A guardian routed into a coach surface is a role-boundary failure whether or not the server refuses it second.

The /board subtree resolves its session once, in this gate. Two boundaries: the platform owner reads the board surface rather than being bounced to a login form it has already satisfied, and a valid session that is not board-shaped goes to its own dashboard instead of /login.

The fabricated-data declaration on the Revenue & Funding Center. Three of its tabs describe records the organisation genuinely has, one click from a live register, so an admin has no way to tell the invented grant from the real one -- and for a 501(c)(3) a fabricated figure copied into a board packet or a funder's report is a false statement made by the organisation. Six tests.

The register and the attendance reporter themselves. Listed here on purpose: a guard on guards that could vanish silently would leave the register unvalidated and every entry below unproven, which is the exact failure this file exists to make loud.
